instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a managed relational database for an order system in one AWS Region. The database must lose no committed write if an Availability Zone fails. If the whole Region fails, the company must be able to recover the database in a second Region, and a loss of a few minutes of writes is acceptable. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Run a self-managed database on EC2 instances in a second AWS Region, and write a custom process that ships the changes every minute.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep a replica of the database in a second AWS Region, with asynchronous replication from the primary database in the first Region.

options.label: C
options.text: Take a snapshot of the database every few minutes, and keep all of the snapshots in the same AWS Region as the database.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep a standby copy of the database in a second Availability Zone of the Region, with synchronous replication from the primary database.

options.label: E
options.text: Keep a standby copy of the database in a second Availability Zone of the Region, with asynchronous replication every few minutes.
